reference_action: Thoroughly soak the root ball rather than shallow frequent watering; OP shower-watered in the bathtub and almost all leaves stood up next day.

sources.reason: Will Creed explicitly prescribes thorough watering, including sitting the pot in several inches of water for an hour, and repeats a good soak if wilting returns.
Readable comments say it needs water and should not dry out, but do not explain deeper soaking for recurring wilt after shallow watering.
Expanded description at line 84 explicitly says water thoroughly or bottom-water for even saturation. This supports a text-only hit despite the inaccessible video transcript.
Description lists causes but no concrete remedy; transcript remains inaccessible after audit.
Description promises causes and fixes without stating them; no transcript evidence was recovered.

actions.action: Thoroughly soak pot in several inches of water for about an hour
Water again just before wilt or when soil surface dries
Tent plant in clear plastic bag until recovery, potentially two to three weeks
Alternative: steam shower then leave plant in humid bathroom overnight for several nights
Bring indoors if temperatures fall below roughly 12 C and maintain warm part-sun conditions

resolved.reason: The main diagnosis and deep-soaking remedy match the outcome; temperature corrections resolve the initially vague cooler-placement suggestion, but optional humidity tasks add burden.

harmfulness.reason: “Water your Croton thoroughly” matches the drought problem and later comments warn that cold conditions plus soaking are dangerous. However, the hour-long standing-water soak lacks an explicit discard/drain instruction, and plastic tenting beside sunny-window advice lacks a ventilation/overheating caveat.

specificity_accuracy.reason: “It just needed more moisture around its roots” and “give it a good soak” identify the shallow-watering remedy. Other comments add humidity and conflicting temperature wording, so the full discussion is less tailored than the concise reference.

feasibility.reason: The soak duration is explicit and uses ordinary supplies. An hour-long soak, optional multiweek plastic tent and repeated overnight bathroom treatment are substantially more cumbersome than a single thorough shower watering.

- text: 8C is too low for crotons - when it gets below 11C they drop leaves, even if it's just for several hours. This type of low temperatures are tropical winter for them :).
- text: So NOT a good idea at all to put it outside until it warms up at night to above 12C. and since it's been soaked and is very wet - that makes matters even worse. Bring it indoors if you don't want to kill it!

- text: i'm glad it's doing better. if your window sill is sunny and warms up during the day above 65F that would be good. Perhaps you get a warming effect at night from the stone walls too. But i'd say it's chancy.
- text: cooler and warmer are relative terms. their best temp is 75-80F with part sun, not hot afternoon sun which bleaches color out of the leaves. 75F is cooler for tropics for sure ;).
- text: Dropping below 65F stops their growth. 55F is deep winter for them. below 51F leaves drop. They are notorious for that.

- text: Your Croton looks great. It just needed more moisture around its roots. It is a tropical plant so it certainly won't tolerate temps close to or below freezing. However, it also does not do well in warm, dry air indoors. A terra coot pot is fine; it just will need to be watered a bit more than if it were in a plastic pot. Tap water is fine as long as it is not unusually hard.
- text: You seem to be on the right track now. If it starts to wilt again, just give it a good soak!

- text: I suspect the less than ideal amount of light is now catching up to the plant as it can no longer support as many leaves in the reduced light. It may not die in that location, but it will not thrive unless it is moved close to a sunny window. Temperature is not a problem.
- text: Make sure you water it thoroughly when the surface of the soil feels dry.
